parts.instruction: You will hear a representative from British Waterways called John Sampson talking about a canal network in England.For questions 7-14, complete the sentences with a word or short phrase.

questions.prompt: The canals were built despite the fact that there was no ________ and very little technology.
From 1790 to 1929, there were many canals that were ________ with each other but which were not uniform in size.
The new union of canals provided a ________ between major industrial cities.
There are plenty of ________ for a variety of wildlife on and around the canals.
Walkers can go to the nearest waterway office to get information on ________ so they can start and end at the same place.
Anglers can fish in the canals and ________.
If you want to go fishing, you must buy a ________.
The waterways authority request that people are ________ towards the canal users.

parts.instruction: You will hear part of a radio interview with the comedian, Lenny Henry. For questions 15-20, choose the answer (A, B, C or D) which fits best according to what you hear.

questions.prompt: Why did Lenny decide to do a degree?

options.label: He was self-conscious because he didn’t have one.
Other actors persuaded him that it was a good idea.
He needed one to further his acting career.
He was impressed by other actors who had been to university.

questions.prompt: What effect has studying for a degree had on Lenny?

options.label: It has developed his ability to think more clearly about his work in general.
It has made him think more seriously about his career.
It has given him the confidence to try for more challenging acting roles.
It causes him a lot of stress when he has to write an essay.

questions.prompt: According to Lenny, how does comedy affect the way people feel?

options.label: It hinders their appreciation of the seriousness of a situation.
It helps them deal with disturbing images.
It makes people more sensitive.
It enables them to laugh at heartbreaking stories.

questions.prompt: What does Lenny say about the work of Comic Relief in Africa?

options.label: People in Africa now have new ways of raising money for themselves.
The task they are facing is too big for them to make a real difference.
People aren’t committed enough yet to the cause.
It should be a steady process to help the local communities.

questions.prompt: What does Lenny say about his visit to Debre Zeit?

options.label: He enjoyed working as a care worker for a while.
He was impressed by Fanti’s bravery despite his illness.
He was moved by the way the people there handled their situation.
He was impressed by the way Fanti praised comic Relief.

questions.prompt: What does Lenny say about writing comedy?

options.label: He hopes that he will soon be a more self-confident writer.
He finds it really easy since starting his degree.
He doesn’t think he’ll ever have the confidence to write something on his own.
He no longer likes working with other writers.
